Lecture Notes

SkewerJAX: Absorption Lines in Cosmological Sightlines

A pedagogical review of photon propagation, absorption processes, summary statistics, and survey analysis of cosmological skewers

Review notes / working draft

Last updated November 12, 2026

Start reading SkewerJAX

Abstract

These notes present a compact but careful review of the main physical and mathematical ingredients involved in the generation of absorption features from gas distributed along cosmological sightlines. Their main purpose is to provide a clear and pedagogical account of the equations governing photon propagation in an expanding universe, the local formation of absorption lines, the construction of optical depth and transmitted flux, and the statistical description of the resulting flux field. Although the Ly\(\alpha\) forest analysis provides a central physical motivation, the discussion is formulated in a sufficiently general way to be useful for related absorption processes as well.

A secondary motivation for these notes is to accompany SkewerJAX, a JAX-based implementation for computing absorption lines from cosmological simulations, lightcones, and related datasets. In that context, the derivations collected here are intended not only as theoretical background, but also as a practical reference connecting the underlying physics to forms that are convenient for numerical implementation. Overall, the goal is to offer a self-contained guide that can help readers build a solid understanding of the relevant equations while also serving as a useful companion for computational work.
